body.statement:
Under the conclusion of the uniform generated-projector expansion, define \(s_{n,k}=Q_Ac_k/\lambda_n\), let \(Z_n=(Z_{n,k})_{k=d+2}^{R_{\max}}\), and set
\[
 \mathfrak L_n(h;z)=\max_{d+2\le k\le R_{\max}}
 \lVert z_k-hs_{n,k}\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 I_n=\sqrt n\lambda_n[-B-\beta,B-\beta].
\]
If \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\), then, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\),
\[
 \sqrt n\lambda_n(\widehat\beta-\beta)=O_{\mathbb P}(1)
\]
and, with \(\widehat h_n=\sqrt n\lambda_n(\widehat\beta-\beta)\),
\[
 \mathfrak L_n(\widehat h_n;Z_n)
 \le \inf_{h\in I_n}\mathfrak L_n(h;Z_n)+o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{14}
\]
Thus the first-order law of the possibly nonsmooth estimator is the argmin functional of a Gaussian-shift criterion, with the box constraint retained; an ordinary Gaussian limit follows only when that argmin functional is locally unique and affine.  In addition, there is a finite constant \(K_0\), depending only on the fixed model envelopes, such that every deterministic choice satisfying \(t_{\alpha_0}^2>K_0/\alpha_0\) yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\ \inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \mathbb P_\theta\bigl(\beta\in\mathcal C_n\bigr)\ge1-\alpha_0. \tag{15}
\]
This calibration remains valid for singular influence covariance and requires no generalized inverse.
body.proof_tex:
For \(b=\beta+h/(\sqrt n\lambda_n)\), linearity in \(b\) and the first helper lemma give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k)
 &=\sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)
   -\frac{h}{\lambda_n}\widehat Q\widehat c_k\\
 &=Z_{n,k}-h\frac{Q_Ac_k}{\lambda_n}
   -\frac{h}{\lambda_n}(\widehat Q\widehat c_k-Q_Ac_k)
   +o_{\mathbb P}(1). 
 \end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
Equations (5) and (8) in the preceding proof, applied to \(\widehat c_k\), imply
\[
 \max_{2\le k\le R_{\max}}
 \lVert\widehat Q\widehat c_k-Q_Ac_k\rVert_2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}) \tag{17}
\]
uniformly.  Therefore, for each fixed \(H<\infty\), \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\) turns (16) into
\[
 \sup_{\lvert h\rvert\le H}\max_k
 \left\lVert
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k)
 -(Z_{n,k}-hs_{n,k})
 \right\rVert_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{18}
\]

The defining shell inequalities give \(1\le\lVert s_{n,r}\rVert_2\le2\).  At \(h=0\), the sample criterion multiplied by \(\sqrt n\) is \(O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), because \(Z_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly by its common second-moment bound.  At the minimizing \(\widehat h_n\), its value is no larger.  Applying the reverse triangle inequality to the \(r\)-th component of (16), and using (17), gives
\[
 \lvert\widehat h_n\rvert
 \le O_{\mathbb P}(1)
 +\frac{\lvert\widehat h_n\rvert}{\sqrt n\lambda_n}O_{\mathbb P}(1). \tag{19}
\]
The last random coefficient is smaller than one half with probability tending uniformly to one, so it can be absorbed into the left side.  Hence \(\widehat h_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  On a compact interval containing \(\widehat h_n\) with arbitrarily high uniform probability, (18) and the minimizing property of \(\widehat\beta\) yield (14).  Because changing every block \(z_k\) by at most \(a\) changes \(\mathfrak L_n(h;z)\) by at most \(a\), the bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian approximation for \(Z_n\) transfers to every bounded Lipschitz functional of the local criterion.  If the Gaussian argmin is unique and separated, the elementary argmin implication
\[
 \sup_{\lvert h\rvert\le H}\lvert f_n(h)-f(h)\rvert\to0,
 \quad
 \inf_{\lvert h-h_0\rvert\ge\varepsilon}f(h)>f(h_0)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathop{\rm argmin}f_n\to h_0
\]
gives the corresponding estimator distribution.  If uniqueness fails or \(\beta\) lies on the boundary, (14), rather than an unjustified normal law, is the valid first-order characterization.

For coverage, define
\[
 S_n=\max_{d+2\le k\le R_{\max}}
 \left\lVert\sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)\right\rVert_2.
\]
The first helper lemma and the moment bounds give a finite \(K_0\) for which
\[
 \limsup_n\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \mathbb E_\theta[S_n^2]\le K_0. \tag{20}
\]
To check the bound without demanding fourth moments, use (5) and the deterministic projector bounds
\[
 \lVert\widehat Q-Q_A\rVert\le2,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat Q-Q_A\rVert\le K\lVert\widehat C-C\rVert
 \quad\text{when }\lVert\widehat C-C\rVert\le\kappa_0/2.
\]
The second bound follows from (7), while Markov's inequality and (5) show that the complementary event has probability \(O(n^{-1})\).  Consequently \(n\mathbb E\lVert(\widehat Q-Q_A)h_k\rVert^2\) is bounded.  The other part, \(\sqrt n\widehat Q[(\widehat m_k-m_k)-\beta(\widehat c_k-c_k)]\), has bounded second moment by (3)--(6) and \(\lVert\widehat Q\rVert\le1\).  This proves (20).  The singleton fallback is used only when the displayed inversion set is empty.  Whether or not that set is empty, failure to cover \(\beta\) implies \(S_n>t_{\alpha_0}\).  Hence Markov's inequality, proved here by
\[
 \mathbb E[S_n^2]\ge t_{\alpha_0}^2
 \mathbb P(S_n>t_{\alpha_0}),
\]
and (20) give
\[
 \limsup_n\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \mathbb P_\theta(\beta\notin\mathcal C_n)
 \le \frac{K_0}{t_{\alpha_0}^2}<\alpha_0. \tag{21}
\]
This proves (15).  Neither (20) nor (21) uses the rank of \(\Sigma_n\), which proves singularity robustness.
body.justification: This lemma converts the corrected moment expansion into a computable local argmin law and a covariance-inversion-free coverage guarantee.
body.gap: A Gaussian moment process need not produce an ordinary Gaussian estimator when the max-norm criterion ties or the effect lies on the compact boundary.
body.consumer: The OEQ resolution uses this lemma to state the sharp form of the estimator approximation and Anderson--Rubin calibration.
